title: The Harivamsha — the Sanskrit text
author: vyasa
attributionNote: The Harivaṃśa is ascribed to Vyasa and transmitted as an appendix to the Mahabharata; its core is later than the epic's narrative books and the text was extended by the Krishna-worshipping communities that read it. GRETIL's e-text is the constituted text with the star passages of the Bhandarkar edition (Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya, Poona 1969) and was entered by a large team of scholars led by Peter Schreiner.
description: The Harivaṃśa is the genealogy of the house of Krishna, told as a continuation of the Mahabharata: the creation and the ages, the solar and lunar lineages, the births of the gods, and then the life of Krishna — his birth in Mathura, the exchange that carried him to Vrindavan, the killing of the tyrant Kamsa, the founding of Dvaraka and his wars, the war of the Pandavas told in brief, and finally the destruction of the Yadavas and the departure of Krishna. Its Vishnu Parvan identifies Krishna with the supreme god and is the earliest long statement of that identification.
historicalContext: The text stands at the point where the epic's hero becomes the object of worship: in it Krishna is narrated as a man of the Yadava house and praised as the god who sustains the world, and the devotional traditions of Mathura and Dvaraka trace their scriptural line to it. It was translated into English as the Harivamsa by Manmatha Nath Dutt and, in the same spirit, by the Poona editors whose constituted text GRETIL follows.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the constituted text with its star passages, the 118 chapters of the Harivaṃśa together with the opening invocation the file numbers 0, 6,071 verses in all, streamed from GRETIL one chapter at a time. The appendix the same edition prints as Appendix I is a separate file in GRETIL and is not published as part of this work, and the reader's notice names the edition being read. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
